subject: AcmeFT: Request for private deployment penetration test evidence & boundary assumptions
messages:
From: Daniel Ruiz <daniel.ruiz@acmeft.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Lee <security@acmeft.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jul 2025 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Penetration test evidence for private deployment (scope and boundary questions)

Hi Evelyn / Marissa,

Thanks for the SOC 2 artifact bundle you shared last week. As we're finishing our procurement review I have two outstanding asks relating to your private deployment option (our deployment will be a VPC peered/private connector model):

1) Do you have a redacted penetration test report or executive summary that covers Redwood Private and the private connector used to attach customer VPCs?
2) Can you explain your boundary assumptions for penetration testing—specifically, what you consider in-scope vs. customer responsibility when the connector sits inside our VPC? We need to be explicit in our security assessment (third-party risk).

If you have a remediation status tracker and a short statement about whether the connector itself was tested in a customer-like environment, that would help us close our SIG/CAIQ questions.

Requested timing: ideally within the next two weeks (we're targeting our security committee on 24 Jul).

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a quick call if that's easier.

Regards,
Daniel
Daniel Ruiz
Head of Security, Acme FinTech
daniel.ruiz@acmeft.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Ruiz <daniel.ruiz@acmeft.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Lee <security@acmeft.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jul 2025 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Penetration test evidence for private deployment (scope and boundary questions)

Hi Daniel — thanks for the clear ask. Short answers up front: we have a redacted executive pen-test summary and a remediation tracker that we can share today; the canonical boundary is that Redwood tests our control and management planes and the connector software itself in a lab/customer-simulated environment, but we do not run tests within a customer's production VPC unless explicitly contracted and coordinated.

Attachments: redwood-pen-test-summary-acmeft-2025-07-redacted.pdf (executive summary, redacted PII) and remediation-tracker-acmeft-2025-07.xlsx (current status).

Details / scope summary:
- In-scope by default: Redwood control plane components (authentication, API endpoints, admin consoles), management plane network interfaces we operate, and the connector binary/source as deployed in our staging lab that mirrors customer config. Tests included network-level scans, authenticated API testing, and privilege escalation checks.
- Out-of-scope by default: Customer-managed network segments (your VPC subnets, KMS, customer storage buckets) and any customer-managed resources that Redwood does not control. When the connector is deployed inside a customer VPC, we treat the VPC boundary as customer-controlled.

What we can offer:
- A redacted summary (attached) showing the key findings and remediation timelines.
- An option to run an on-site/inside-VPC pen test through our third-party partner (SecureScan Labs) under a scoped engagement. In that case, testing in your VPC would be explicitly in-scope and the engagement would be run under a separate SoW.

If you need a one-paragraph statement for SIG/CAIQ: "Redwood's internal penetration tests cover the Redwood-managed control and management planes and the connector software in a customer-simulated environment. Testing within a customer's VPC is performed only under a separately contracted engagement and coordinated with the customer's security operations team."

I'll loop in our infra and solutions teams to confirm specifics for the connector used in your deployment.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Solutions Security | Redwood Inference
evelyn_hart@redwood.ai

From: Daniel Ruiz <daniel.ruiz@acmeft.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Lee <security@acmeft.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 13 Jul 2025 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Penetration test evidence for private deployment (scope and boundary questions)

Thanks Evelyn — that helps a lot. Couple of clarifying points:

- Our security team specifically wants to know whether the private connector (agent process that runs in our VPC and establishes outbound TLS to Redwood) was exercised against real network ACLs and customer-like IAM policies during your last engagement, or whether testing was limited to a lab environment with simulated VPC networking.
- If testing was lab-only, would Redwood be able to support an inside-VPC test where Redwood or a third party performs authenticated testing against the connector within our environment? We understand this requires scheduling and an SoW, but want to confirm feasibility and a high-level timeline for that work.

CC'ing our security lead Sarah for visibility.

Daniel

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Penetration test evidence for private deployment (AcmeFT) — confirm connector scope

Karthik / Jonas — forwarding Daniel's questions above. He wants to know definitively whether our last pen test exercised the connector in a customer-like VPC (network ACLs, IAM constraints) or if it was limited to the lab. He also asks whether we can coordinate an inside-VPC authenticated test through SecureScan. Please reply with:
1) What exactly was tested relative to the connector in the latest 2025-06/05 pen test (lab vs customer-simulated).
2) Any technical/operational constraints we should tell the customer (e.g., required ports, testing windows, who must be present in their SOC).
3) Rough cost / timeline if we run an on-site inside-VPC pen test via SecureScan (please include any minimum engagement length and expected remediation SLA).

Thanks — we need an answer to get back to Acme by 22 Jul.

—Evelyn

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Jul 2025 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FW: Penetration test evidence for private deployment (AcmeFT) — confirm connector scope

Evelyn — quick summary from infra/security testing team:

1) The June 2025 full pen test included the connector software in scope, but testing was performed in our staging lab that mirrors common customer network configurations. Network ACLs and IAM policies were simulated; we did not run active tests inside any customer production VPC.

2) Constraints for inside-VPC testing:
   - We require a dedicated test window (typ. 2–5 business days) and a single point-of-contact in the customer's SOC for real-time coordination.
   - Required outbound ports: 443 (TLS), and the connector health port 9100 (if enabled). Any customer-managed firewall rules that block outbound TLS interception must be disclosed pre-test.
   - We cannot perform destructive testing against customer data stores; tests focus on authentication authorization, lateral movement from the connector host, and privilege escalation attempts.

3) Cost / timeline via SecureScan:
   - Minimum engagement: 3 business days on-site access + 2 days of analysis and report prep.
   - Typical turnaround: 10 business days from start to delivery of a redacted executive summary + full technical report under NDA.
   - Estimated price band (ballpark): $35k–$55k depending on scope (authenticated tests + web app checks + infrastructure checks).
   - Remediation SLA: We offer a 30/60/90 tracking cadence — critical fixes target 30 days; medium/low are tracked in the remediation workbook.

I've attached proposed-connector-scope-2025-07.docx which we can adapt into an SoW. If Acme wants Redwood personnel present during testing, we can add that to the SoW.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Infrastructure & Security Engineering | Redwood Inference

Daniel / Sarah — thanks for your patience. Attached is the redacted executive summary and our current remediation tracker. Per Karthik's note, the connector was tested in a customer-simulated lab environment in June; it was not exercised inside a live customer VPC.

Proposed next steps (we can iterate based on your needs):
1) Scope confirmation call (30 min) — we align on what you want tested inside your VPC and agree on SOW items (Redwood personnel presence, types of authenticated tests).
2) SecureScan engagement — SecureScan can run the on-site authenticated testing during a 3–5 day window. We've looped them in on this thread; ops@securescan.com, please confirm availability and any additional requirements.
3) Deliverables and cadence — SecureScan delivers a redacted exec summary + full technical report to Acme under NDA; Redwood will provide a remediation plan and track fixes in the remediation-tracker-acmeft-2025-07.xlsx with SLAs as noted earlier.

If this sounds reasonable I can have a draft SoW issued to you (link attached) and schedule the kick-off. For your security committee on 24 Jul, the short statement you can use is: "Redwood's internal pen testing covers Redwood-managed components and the connector in simulated environments; Redwood offers on-site inside-VPC testing through a third-party partner under a scoped SoW."

Best,

- Temporary test account credentials for the connector host and a short-lived API key for authenticated tests
